newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa sits up, speaks, but still weak.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa sits up, speaks, but still weak.

text.p: Mother Teresa was strong enough on Thursday to emerge from bed for the first time this week, but she still remained in critical condition in an Indian heart clinic, her doctors said.

"Mother Teresa ... is critically ill but some vital signs remain stable. Her heart rhythm is irregular but the rate is controlled," doctors at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in an evening bulletin on her health.
They again delayed an X-ray test, saying that the legendary Roman Catholic nun was not yet strong enough.
"She is not as yet fit for the angiography," said Dr Tarun Praharaj, one of her doctors.
Praharaj told reporters Mother Teresa, who was admitted to hospital last Friday with an irregular heartbeat, appeared to be cheerful and in good spirits.
"For the first time since Friday she moved out of bed and sat on a chair for half-an-hour," he added. "She spoke to some nuns and the doctors."
Earlier, doctors had delayed at least until Friday an angiography X-ray procedure to determine whether surgery was needed. "We may do it tomorrow or Sunday," Praharaj said.
The test uses an X-ray and an opaque dye injected into blood vessels to check for arterial blockage.
There were indications that Mother Teresa required surgery, her cardiologist, Dr A.K. Bardhan, said.
"All indications lead to the conclusion that she has a blockage in her coronary artery," Bardhan said.
Mother Teresa had no chest pain since she last underwent heart surgery in 1993, Bardhan said.
"But what happened last Friday was serious heart failure and chest pain. Therefore angioplasty is almost certain. Let us see when the doctors can conduct the angiography," he added.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
She has undergone coronary angiography twice -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
Each time she also had angioplasty, in which surgeons insert a balloon into an artery and inflate it to unblock the artery.
Mother Teresa was moved to the Birla centre on Tuesday from the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home.
Mother Teresa's heart problem later worsened and her doctors delayed the angiography, originally planned for Wednesday.
Meanwhile, members of the Missionaries of Charity, the religious order Mother Teresa founded in 1949, prayed for the recovery of the 1979 Nobel Peace prize winner.
"We are having prayers all over the world for her recovery," Sister Priscilla, the order's spokeswoman, said.
The charity, devoted to the poor, destitute and dying, has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries.
Britain's Independent newspaper reported on Wednesday that Mother Teresa had begged her doctors to let her die.
"She talked very openly about not wanting to live any longer," the Independent quoted Jim Towey, a former seminarian with the Missionaries of Charity, as saying.
Albanian President Sali Berisha conferred the nation's top "Honour of the Nation" decoration on his diminutive compatriot on Albania's national day on Thursday.
"We give the award to the most renowned Albanian of all times, the living saint of our nation, Mother Teresa," he said.
"It is a sign of the deep gratitude the Albanian nation nurtures for the Missionary of God, the symbol of love and hope, its honour and pride," Berisha added.
